To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel reduced entropy condition variational auto-encoder for the unsupervised recovery from corrupted data, that we show its superior performance in different data sets, and that we demonstrate its ability to propagate uncertainty to downstream classification tasks.

we propose a new probabilis-tic method for unsupervi-sed recovery of cor-rupted data, and we show that this method performs better in data imputation and de-nosing than existing variational approaches.

1) our model can accurately recover the clean data and the underlying uncertainty from a large set of degraded samples; 2) our model is more accurate than the existing methods; 3) our model can be used to propagate the underlying uncertainty to downstream tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unsupervised recovery and imputation of missing data in a probabilistic framework.
the problem of unsupervised recovery and characterisation of corrupted data.
the problem of unsupervised Bayesian data recovery from incomplete data sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we propose a novel probabilistic method for the unsupervised recovery and reconstruction of corrupted data, which is able to accurately characterise the uncertainty of the recovered values, allowing for the exploration of the space of possible reconstructed data.
our method is a powerful and flexible framework for the unsupervised recovery and imputation of missing values and noisy data.

we present a novel method that can recover accurate posteriors in a wide range of data recovery tasks, including missing values, noise and outliers, and can be easily adapted to a wide range of problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel probabilistic method for data imputation and de-nosing that is able to recover rich posterior densities of clean values.
we propose an unsupervised Bayesian method for recovering corrupted data that results in rich posterior distributions, and hence characterises the underlying uncertainty.
our proposed model can recover corrupted data and propagate the recovered uncertainty to downstream tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by using our new variational framework, we can recover accurate posterior densities for the clean values of the data, allowing for the exploration of the solution space and the propagation of uncertainty to downstream tasks.
, when the data is corrupted, a probabilistic model should be able to capture the uncertainty in the recovered data, which is a crucial aspect for the success of the downstream task.
, when dealing with large ensembles of data, it is possible to recover accurate posteriors of corrupted data, without the need for any supervision or additional training data.
